title: Make API coverage reporting use the same authoritative ledger as coverage tests
description:
## Finding

Production `api coverage` reports CLI coverage as 55/92 while the test ledger reports 88/92. Separate hard-coded tables make the diagnostic untrustworthy and allow drift.

## Evidence at audited commit

`crates/thegn-host/src/cmd/api.rs:66` and `crates/thegn-host/src/cmd/session.rs:1945`.

## Implementation constraints

Derive CLI and test reporting from one route/command coverage registry; classify intentional exclusions with machine-readable reasons.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CLI, tests, and generated docs report identical numerators/denominators for the same revision.
- [ ] Every uncovered operation has one stable reason/category and owner or explicit non-goal.
- [ ] Adding/removing a command or route requires updating one authority and fails drift tests otherwise.
- [ ] Human and JSON output include revision/schema version.
- [ ] Regression tests lock the current counts only through generated data, not duplicate literals.

## Execution dependencies

Blocked by THE-190 — LANDED on main, so this is unblocked. Directly blocks THE-201, THE-204, THE-203, THE-202.
